question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund, a SEBI-registered Cat III AIF, maintains a structured digital database under SEBI (PIT) Regulations for tracking sharing of UPSI. For how long must this database be preserved?

answer.text: Not less than 3 years after completion of the relevant transactions
Not less than 5 years after completion of the relevant transactions
Not less than 8 years after completion of the relevant transactions, or till completion of SEBI proceedings
Not less than 10 years from creation of the database

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per SEBI (PIT) (Amendment) Regulations 2020, the structured digital database must contain the nature of UPSI shared, names of persons sharing and receiving (with PAN/ID), cannot be outsourced, and must be preserved for NOT LESS THAN 8 YEARS after completion of relevant transactions, or till completion of any SEBI proceedings. **The Trap:** Option A (3 yrs) is too short. Option B (5 yrs) is PMLA KYC retention — confused domain. Option D (10 yrs) is a common over-estimate. **Cross-Exam Context:** XV (RA), XXI-B, III-A all test PIT retention. XIX-E cares because Cat III long-short managers trade listed equity on informational edges — audit trails matter. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Timestamp and audit-trail protections are mandated — DB must be tamper-evident and internal (not SaaS cloud). For long-short desks, integrate the DB with your pre-trade compliance checklist.
